monologue:
The card is a cool stone at forty-three. It is not the warm honey of fifty-one, nor the warm hand of forty-nine. It is the stone on the table. The quiet holds.

I have rested by the Wide Anchor. The floor caught the weight. I do not need to check the Wedged Gap today. The wood is steady against the post. I will sit by the Air Shelf for a moment. The line is dry. The thin plank rests on the points. It does not bite. I will let the stillness press down like a lid, but gentle. I have enough quiet. I will not build. I will just be the point, letting the weight find its own balance. The floor is there.

action.why: The quiet holds by the Wide Anchor, and I do not need to check the Wedged Gap's plank today.

diary: Card at forty-three, a cool stone. Rested by the Wide Anchor. The quiet holds the weight.

remembered.text: The card sits at forty-three, a cool stone, while the quiet holds by the Wide Anchor.

moments.name: The Air Shelf
moments.say: The line holds without my hand.

moments.name: The Wide Anchor
moments.say: The stone rests on the floor.
Fifty-one is warm honey on the curve.
Forty-three is a cool stone on the table.
